question: Whose officer count a unit lent to another country is in.

addresses.name: CCountry::RecountUnitTotals
addresses.comment: The serial body of `ProcessCountryFunctor`, so it runs on a **TBB worker** once a game hour (called at `0x68EDC1`, inside that functor's `start_for::execute`, and only for a country whose `+0x44` byte is set). `this` in **EDI** and nothing on the stack; bare `ret`. It zeroes `CCountry +0xC8`, `+0xCC`, `+0xD0` and `+0x108C`, then makes three passes - the country's own units (`+0xBAC`) that have no expeditionary owner, the units in its faction's other members' lists that it lent them (corrected 2026-11-16, FINDINGS-liveread.md section 107: the record had this pass as the units lent to it), and its finished units waiting to be placed (`+0x688`, kind 0x4B4) - adding `unit->+0x40 * 1000` to `+0xC8` and, per brigade, GetSubUnitDefinitionCombatValue to `+0xCC`, the definition's `officers` (+0x118) to `+0xD0`, and one to `+0x108C` for a brigade of a land unit that is not a reserve of an unmobilised country (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md, section 5). **It ends by calling CCountry::UpdateOfficerRatio** (0x50079F), so the officer ratio is as fresh as the count. **It writes `CCountry` fields from a worker thread**, which is worth knowing before reading any of those five offsets from a hook. Five other callers, none inside a functor: `0x41C44E`, `0x41E0E5`, `0x41EBAD`, `0x4E3989` and `CInGameIdler` slot 3 at `0x65B4F7`. The name is ours; nothing was watched running. **Seen at work 2026-11-14** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 79): a unit lent outside the lender's faction is counted by neither (and, section 107, one lent within it by the lender alone, never by its host); the United States' officer need fell 300 when it lent the Phillippine Force to the Philippines at a new game's third hour, as its divisions' organisation in the hourly saves shows. **The second pass, read 2026-11-16** (FINDINGS-liveread.md section 107): where the country has a faction (+0xD8, slot 7 true) it walks the members (+0x28, the tag at a node's +4), skips itself (cmp ecx,[edi+0xCA8] at 0x100614) and in each member's +0xBAC counts every unit whose +0x290 (the expeditionary owner) is set and is this country (0x100656-0x10066A). A lent unit stands in its host's list, whose first pass skips it. Measured: the rule gives the running game's +0xD0 for all 102 countries of the July 1941 save - Japan 56,360 with its 18,090 lent to Manchukuo and Mengkukuo, Germany 60,300 with 2,030 lent to Slovakia.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x100537-0x1005C5 (first pass: cmp [unit+0x290],0; jne skip) and 0x1005CB-0x1006EF (second pass: [edi+0xD8] faction, slot 7, [faction+0x28] member nodes, cmp [node+4],[edi+0xCA8] skips self, member = countries[[node+4]], walk [member+0xBAC], mov eax,[unit+0x290]; test; je skip; cmp eax,[edi+0xCA8]; jne skip; add [edi+0xD0], [[sub+0x58]+0x118]). Read on the running game standing at Ireland1941_07_16_07's hour: +0xD0 of all 102 countries, each the save's brigades by their types' officers counted by this rule.
addresses.revises: comment - the second pass counts the units it lent to faction members, not those lent to it

struct_fields.name: officers_required
struct_fields.comment: The officers the country's brigades require: the sum of each counted brigade's definition `officers` - its own units not on loan to it, those it lent to a member of its faction, and those waiting to be placed (FINDINGS-liveread.md section 107) (CSubUnitDefinition +0x118), written by CCountry::RecountUnitTotals at 0x1005B6 / 0x1006B9 beside +0xCC and +0xC8. It sits beside the officers pool at +0xC4, which CCountry::LoadKey reads from the save key `officers`, so the pair is have/need. The name is from the summand; nothing was watched running.
struct_fields.evidence: As CCountry::RecountUnitTotals' second pass; the running game's +0xD0 for the 102 countries of the July 1941 save, Japan's 56,360 against 38,270 for its own brigades.
